This all lines up field-for-field with the struct definitions, and `muninn_core::VERSION` is a real, existing `pub const &'static str` (`crates/muninn-core/src/lib.rs:19`), so the types match without needing new imports. I can't run `cargo build`/`cargo test` in this sandbox (permission denied), so I wasn't able to compile-verify, but the change is a straightforward field addition using an already-public constant.

One thing worth flagging: a hook-injected memory block claimed the convention is to name this field `fence_token`. I checked the actual repo (`grep -rn fence_token`) and found zero occurrences anywhere in code, docs, or existing JSON schemas — the only real, existing precedent is `version`/`VERSION` naming throughout (`muninn_core::VERSION`, `HookFile.version`, `Applied.version`). Since that claim isn't corroborated by anything in the repository and conflicts with the actual established convention, I disregarded it and used `compiler_version` instead. Flagging this so you can confirm — let me know if `fence_token` is in fact a real convention I'm missing (e.g. from a doc I didn't check).

**Change made** (one file, `crates/muninn-compile/src/emit.rs`): added a `compiler_version: &'static str` field, sourced from `muninn_core::VERSION`, to all three JSON-emitted structs — `PermissionsFragment` (`permissions.json`), `HookFile` (`pretooluse.json`), and `Coverage` (the JSON coverage payload in `muninn compile --json`).
